question: Should the Windows cleanup safeguards also reject previously accepted multiline or shell-ambiguous script commands unconditionally?
rationale: Rejecting those forms may reduce uncertainty during ancestry verification, but it changes the existing script-command contract and can break working configurations during upgrade; tests cannot determine the intended compatibility policy.

options.title: Preserve Compatibility
options.body: Keep existing command forms accepted by default while failing closed only when cleanup cannot prove the target process identity.

options.title: Add Opt-In Strictness
options.body: Introduce an explicit strict setting that rejects ambiguous command forms while retaining current behavior for existing configurations.

options.title: Accept Breaking Strictness
options.body: Reject the command forms unconditionally and require clear upgrade documentation plus fresh-install and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Preserve Compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep existing command forms accepted by default while failing closed only when cleanup cannot prove the target process identity.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch author is a repository member with security-domain context and has carried the complete refinement sequence for this behavior.
